P0500.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0500.description: The vehicle speed signal A comes, depending on the maker, from a sensor on the gearbox, the transmission output speed, the wheel speeds via ABS/ESP or a CAN message; CARB explicitly names it as an input to be monitored. P0500 is the general code for this signal. Ford checks plausibility: the car must be moving (high load, positive torque), yet the signal stays below 1–5 mph for 5 s; Ford diesels flag a missing CAN message after 0.5 s. GM's Saturn ION of 2004 used high load with below 3 mph for 6.2 s (MIL after two trips); GM's 2018 tables use P0502/P0503 instead. Cruise control is then disabled and substitute values are used.

causes.label: ABS/ESP module or wheel speed sensor faulty (signal source)
Output speed sensor or vehicle speed sensor faulty or dirty (metal debris on the magnet)
Wire or connector open or shorted, corrosion
CAN communication fault (message missing)
Wrong tyre or axle data programmed

P0501.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0501.description: The vehicle speed signal A comes, depending on the maker, from a sensor on the gearbox, the transmission output speed, the wheel speeds via ABS/ESP or a CAN message; CARB explicitly names it as an input to be monitored. P0501 means the signal is present but does not fit the driving state or lies outside the physically possible range. Saab's Trionic T5 sets it above 270 km/h; other makers typically compare it with engine speed times gear ratio, wheel speeds or the transmission output speed. GM's 2018 tables and Ford do not use P0501 (GM: P0503, Ford: P0500). Cruise control is then disabled.

causes.label: Wheel speed sensor or tone ring damaged or dirty (ABS source)
Wrong tyre size, axle ratio or coding
Sensor with weak signal or damaged tone wheel
Interference from damaged shielding or ground

P0502.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P0502.description: The vehicle speed signal A comes, depending on the maker, from a sensor on the gearbox, the transmission output speed, the wheel speeds via ABS/ESP or a CAN message; CARB explicitly names it as an input to be monitored. Despite its wording, all makers found check plausibility: the car is clearly moving (load, torque, overrun), yet the signal stays at zero. GM's 2018 tables use the transmission output speed: below 12 rpm (petrol) or 60 rpm (diesel) for 4.5 s, MIL on the first trip. Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X) sets it below 1 km/h on overrun for over 4 s with the MIL at once; Saab's T5 after 4 s without signal above 1800 rpm. Electrical faults give the same picture.

causes.label: Speed or output speed sensor faulty
Wire open or shorted to ground, connector corroded
ABS module sends no speed signal
Tone wheel damaged or sensor dirty

P0503.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic/High
P0503.description: The vehicle speed signal A comes, depending on the maker, from a sensor on the gearbox, the transmission output speed, the wheel speeds via ABS/ESP or a CAN message; CARB explicitly names it as an input to be monitored. P0503 combines three fault patterns: sporadic signal loss, jumping values and a value that is too high. GM detects a sudden signal drop quickly (0.3 s, 5 counts, MIL on the first trip); Subaru sets it at 240 km/h or more for a cumulative 4 s, Saab's diesel above 220 km/h. In limp mode Subaru sets the speed to zero, disables fuel cut-off on overrun and raises the fan.

causes.label: Loose contact, chafed wire, corroded connector
Interference from damaged shielding or the ignition
Sensor with weakened magnet or damaged tone wheel
ABS/ESP fault (signal source)

symptoms: Cruise control drops out, jerky shifting

P0504.title: Brake Switch A/B Correlation
P0504.description: The brake pedal switch has two contacts – A usually for the brake lights, B for cruise control and brake information – working in opposite sense, so the module expects opposite states on every brake application. P0504 means they disagree. The signal is used for cruise control cut-off, brake override with electronic throttle, the shift interlock and start-stop. Ford sets it only after more than 25 (petrol) or 40 (diesel) disagreeing brake applications, with the wrench lamp instead of the warning lamp; a NHTSA investigation covers Hyundai brake light switches.

causes.label: Brake light switch faulty (burnt or corroded contact)
Switch misadjusted or retaining clip or stop pad worn
Wire, connector or brake light fuse faulty
Moisture in fuse or junction boxes

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be switched on
Brake lights stay on or do not come on
Selector lever cannot be moved out of P

P0505.title: Idle Control System
P0505.description: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0505 is the general fault of the idle control, used where the maker does not separate too low from too high or the control is at its limit. With an idle valve it is typically sticking or gummed (Saab T5: idle outside 700–1200 rpm); on electronic throttles a Ford investigation shows P0505 from deposits in the throttle body. Ford's 2020–23 engines disable start-stop with P0505–P0507. Warning lamp behaviour depends on the maker.

causes.label: Throttle body or idle valve dirty or gummed
False air (hoses, intake gasket, crankcase ventilation)
Idle valve faulty mechanically or electrically
Learned values not reset after cleaning

symptoms: Idle speed fluctuates, too high or too low
Engine stalls at idle or when coasting

P0506.title: Idle Control System RPM - Lower Than Expected
P0506.description: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0506 means the idle speed of the warm engine at standstill stays too low despite fully used control. GM uses more than 91 rpm filtered for 10 s (MIL after two trips), Ford petrol −100 rpm plus a correction above 1 lb/min, Ford diesel −100 rpm for 5 s, Subaru −100 rpm with the correction at its limit for 10 s three times. Typical are deposits, extra load or a restricted intake or exhaust.

causes.label: Deposits at the throttle or bypass channel, or gummed idle valve
Extra load: stiff accessory drive, gearbox or converter
Intake or exhaust restricted (air filter, catalyst)
Idle valve or throttle actuator faulty, wrong learned value
Mechanical engine damage (low compression)

symptoms: Engine stalls when stopping or with A/C on
Check engine light after two trips

P0507.title: Idle Control System RPM - Higher Than Expected
P0507.description: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0507 means the idle speed stays above target although the control is at its minimum – air bypasses the control or the throttle does not close. GM uses more than 182 rpm filtered (MIL after two trips), Ford petrol +200 rpm, Ford diesel +160 rpm, Subaru +200 rpm for 10 s three times; on the Saab 9-4X three overspeed fuel cut-offs at standstill also set it. False air is the classic cause.

causes.label: False air (vacuum hose, intake gasket, brake booster)
Crankcase ventilation leaking or wrongly routed
Throttle not closing fully (deposits, ice, stop misadjusted)
Idle valve stuck open
Wrong throttle learned value after cleaning or replacement

P0508.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low
P0508.description: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0508 is an electrical fault in the drive circuit of a separate idle valve. Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X) feeds the valve from the main relay and pulses it to ground; the module counts signal edges and sets P0508 at 8 or fewer in 64 ms instead of about 160 – the output hangs at one level – with the warning lamp at once and limp mode without idle control. Many makers, Ford among them, report all circuit faults under P0511 instead.

causes.label: Idle valve coil faulty
Control wire shorted to ground or open
Supply missing (main relay, fuse)
Connector contact at valve or module
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on at once

P0509.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit High
P0509.description: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0509 is the counterpart of P0508: the drive circuit of the idle valve is shorted to positive or shows implausibly many signal edges – Subaru sets it at 225 or more in 64 ms, with the warning lamp at once and limp mode without idle feedback. It only exists on engines with a separate idle valve.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to positive
Idle valve with shorted turns
Connector corroded or wet, interference
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light on at once

P050A.title: Cold Start Idle Control System Performance
P050A.description: After a cold start the engine module raises idle speed and air mass and retards the ignition so that much heat goes into the exhaust and the catalyst lights off quickly. CARB requires this cold-start strategy to be monitored with its own codes, separate from ordinary idle and ignition faults. Ford collects data during the first 15 s after a cold start (coolant and catalyst 20–100 °F) and judges after 300 s, once per trip. P050A checks whether the raised idle speed or air mass commanded at a cold start is actually reached: Ford sets it when the average deviation between target and actual speed exceeds 200 rpm, with the warning lamp. GM does not use P050A as its own monitor and reports cold-start system faults under its manufacturer code P1400.

causes.label: Throttle or idle valve dirty or coked, not enough air when cold
False air or vacuum leak
Fault in the throttle or idle valve circuit
Extra load at cold start (alternator, A/C), stiff engine

symptoms: Idle after a cold start too low, too high or hunting
Occasional stalling shortly after a cold start

P050B.title: Cold Start Ignition Timing Performance
P050B.description: After a cold start the engine module raises idle speed and air mass and retards the ignition so that much heat goes into the exhaust and the catalyst lights off quickly. CARB requires this cold-start strategy to be monitored with its own codes, separate from ordinary idle and ignition faults. Ford collects data during the first 15 s after a cold start (coolant and catalyst 20–100 °F) and judges after 300 s, once per trip. P050B checks the ignition part of the strategy – the retard for catalyst heating; CARB allows checking only the commanded value. Ford sets it when desired and commanded cold-start timing differ by more than 10°, for example because knock, torque or idle control take back the retard. FCA fixed P050B on the 2.0-litre turbo Wrangler of 2018–19 with software. GM has no separate monitor.

causes.label: Engine module software or calibration
Idle control takes back the retard because speed would drop (false air, dirty throttle)
Knock control or knock sensor intervenes
Extra load or alternator at cold start

symptoms: Catalyst warms up more slowly after a cold start

P050C.title: Cold Start Engine Coolant Temperature Performance
P050C.description: P050C is documented only on Bosch ME9 in the Saab 9-3 V6 2.8 turbo: a cold-start plausibility check of the coolant temperature sensor. After a long stop coolant and intake air must read about the same; the code sets if coolant is more than 10 °C below or 15 °C above intake air, once per trip with the warning lamp. A wrong coolant reading distorts cold-start enrichment and can run the fan on a cold engine. The common reading 'coolant warms up too slowly' does not fit – that is P0125/P0128. GM, Ford and FCA do not use P050C.

causes.label: Coolant temperature sensor drifting, wrong characteristic
Contact resistance or corrosion at the coolant or intake air sensor connector
Intake air temperature sensor reading wrong
Auxiliary heater or block heater not recognised, very short stop

symptoms: Rough running after a cold start
Radiator fan runs with a cold engine

P050D.title: Cold Start Rough Idle
P050D.description: GM's direct-injection petrol engines (from about 2016) split the injection into two pulses and retard the ignition after a cold start to heat the catalyst. P050D counts engine cycles with incomplete combustion via the crankshaft misfire detection during this strategy; if the rate reaches the catalyst-damaging misfire threshold, the code sets – once per trip, while the strategy is active (under 45 s running, coolant up to 66 °C). Mostly MIL after two trips, some calibrations without MIL. Ford and FCA do not use P050D.

causes.label: Injector with poor spray pattern or deposits, or injector circuit fault
Spark plug or ignition coil weak
Engine module software or calibration
Poor fuel or low fuel pressure

symptoms: Check engine light on (depending on calibration)
Rough idle or jerking in the first seconds after a cold start

P050E.title: Cold Start Engine Exhaust Temperature Too Low
P050E.description: After a cold start the engine module raises idle speed and air mass and retards the ignition so that much heat goes into the exhaust and the catalyst lights off quickly. CARB requires this cold-start strategy to be monitored with its own codes, separate from ordinary idle and ignition faults. Ford collects data during the first 15 s after a cold start (coolant and catalyst 20–100 °F) and judges after 300 s, once per trip. P050E is the system check of the strategy: does enough heat reach the exhaust and catalyst? Ford uses no exhaust temperature sensor but a catalyst temperature model – actual against target – and sets the code when the temperature deficit divided by the target rise exceeds 0.4, with the warning lamp. FCA uses P050E on the 3.0-litre EcoDiesel (Ram 1500, Grand Cherokee 2014), where it concerns heating the oxidation catalyst, fixed by software. GM uses its manufacturer code P1400 instead.

causes.label: Idle or air control does not reach the cold-start target (dirty throttle, false air)
Ignition not retarded enough (knock or torque intervention)
Engine module software
Air mass meter reading wrong

P050F.title: Brake Assist Vacuum Too Low
P050F.description: GM (from about model year 2017/18) monitors the brake booster with a vacuum sensor: with the pedal at rest and high intake vacuum the booster must hold its vacuum; a loss over time is filtered as a drift ratio, and above a threshold P050F sets, MIL after two trips. It runs with the engine on, during start-stop auto-stops and after switch-off. Without enough brake vacuum the module must throttle, restart the engine from auto-stop or request a pump – which affects idle and start-stop – and brake assistance can drop. Ford and FCA do not use P050F.

causes.label: Leaking vacuum hose or check valve
Leaking diaphragm in the brake booster
Vacuum sensor or its seal faulty
Electric or mechanical vacuum pump weak (where fitted)

symptoms: Hard brake pedal, especially after auto-stop
Hissing at the pedal, start-stop stops less often

P0510.title: Closed Throttle Position Switch
P0510.description: Older engines with a mechanical throttle have a separate idle contact on the throttle or the combined throttle position sensor (Bosch Motronic throttle switch, Nissan and Toyota sensors with idle switch). The module uses it to recognise idle – for idle control, fuel cut-off on overrun and idle ignition timing – and as a substitute if the position sensor fails. P0510 flags an implausible switch: closed with the throttle open, or open at idle. Manufacturer thresholds were not found in accessible documents; with electronic throttle the switch no longer exists.

causes.label: Idle switch or throttle sensor misadjusted
Switch contacts worn, dirty or corroded
Wire or connector open or shorted
Throttle not closing (deposits, sticking cable, stop misadjusted)
Value not relearned after replacement

symptoms: No fuel cut-off on overrun (higher consumption)

P0511.title: Idle Air Control Circuit
P0511.description: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0511 is the general circuit fault of the idle valve – open, short to ground or to positive – without separating low and high, which CARB permits. Ford (up to about 2012, engines with an idle valve) has the output stage report it via a diagnostic status bit, continuously. Valve types are PWM solenoid or rotary valves (two wires) or stepper motors (four wires, typical of GM). Without a working valve the engine runs on a fixed bypass or the mechanical stop and may stall.

causes.label: Idle valve faulty (coil open or shorted)
Wire open or shorted
Connector corroded, pins pushed back
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Idle too high, too low or fluctuating

P0512.title: Starter Request Circuit
P0512.description: The engine module reads a start request – from the ignition switch, a start button via the body module, or start-stop – and drives the starter relay with it. P0512 flags a fault in this signal. Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X) checks plausibility: if the engine runs above 500 rpm and the start signal stays active for more than 3 minutes, a short or sticking switch is assumed, MIL after two trips. On a Jeep Cherokee diesel a chafed harness caused P0512 with a no-start. The starter then does not crank – or with a short to positive keeps running.

causes.label: Ignition or start switch, or start button, faulty or sticking
Harness chafed, short to ground or positive
Selector or clutch switch in the start path
Starter relay sticking

symptoms: Engine does not start, starter does not crank
Starter keeps running after the start (noise)
Check engine light (Subaru after two trips)

P0513.title: Incorrect Immobilizer Key
P0513.description: The engine module receives a secret code from the immobiliser or body module (Chrysler SKIM/SKREEM/RF hub, Saab CIM); if it does not match the stored code, P0513 sets and starting is prevented – Saab cuts fuel and blocks the starter. The most common trigger is a replaced or reflashed engine module that was not taught to the immobiliser (FCA, Saab), less often handshake timing on FCA hybrids or a key not programmed. FCA lists it as invalid SKIM key. It is not emission-related; CARB does not require immobiliser monitoring, and no source documents a warning lamp.

causes.label: Engine module replaced or reflashed and not taught to the immobiliser
Key or transponder not programmed or faulty
Immobiliser, body or RF hub module replaced or faulty
Software fault in the handshake

symptoms: Engine does not start or stops after 1–2 s

P0514.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0514.description: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0514 is the plausibility check of the temperature signal. On FCA/Alfa Romeo the temperature comes from the intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal; P0514 means its value is implausible, and several cases on the Alfa Giulia 2.0 were fixed by engine module software. A fixed substitute temperature is then used; CARB requires plausibility faults to have their own code.

causes.label: Engine module software (false trigger)
Battery sensor or NTC drifting
Corrosion at sensor or connector near the battery acid
Sensor fitted wrongly after a battery change

symptoms: Charging voltage too high or too low

P0515.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0515.description: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0515 is its general circuit fault – open or short – without separating low and high; the charging voltage is then fixed or conservative. No manufacturer document available to us names this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules. A fixed substitute temperature is then used.

causes.label: Sensor or connector corroded (battery acid)
Wire open or chafed
Sensor not plugged in after a battery change
Module

P0516.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0516.description: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0516 means the signal voltage stays below its limit for a minimum time; with an NTC in a voltage divider a low voltage means very hot, or more often a signal line shorted to ground or an internal short. The module then assumes a hot battery and may charge too little. No manufacturer document available to us names this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules. A fixed substitute temperature is then used.

causes.label: Signal line shorted to ground (chafed at the battery tray)
Sensor shorted internally
Moisture or acid in the connector
Module

symptoms: Battery weak, starting problems in the cold

P0517.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0517.description: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0517 means the signal voltage is above its limit, close to the reference; with an NTC that means very cold, or more often an open circuit – sensor unplugged, wire broken – or a short to positive. The module then assumes a cold battery and may charge too high. No manufacturer document available to us names this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules. A fixed substitute temperature is then used.

causes.label: Sensor unplugged or forgotten after a battery change
Wire or connector open or corroded
Sensor open internally
Signal line shorted to positive

P0518.title: Idle Air Control Circuit Intermittent
P0518.description: Older engines without electronic throttle have a separate idle air control valve bypassing the closed throttle; CARB requires its output to be checked but not the fault types to be coded separately. P0518 means its circuit fails sporadically – the signal or current briefly leaves its valid range and returns. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0518; GM and Ford report idle valve faults as P0505–P0507 and P0511. Engines with electronic throttle do not set it.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the idle valve connector
Broken or chafed wire in the harness
Valve coil with shorted turns (temperature-dependent)
Driver in the engine module

symptoms: Engine stalls when coasting or stopping
Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0519.title: Idle Air Control System Performance
P0519.description: P0519 means the idle control fails functionally with an electrically sound circuit – the actual idle speed deviates strongly despite fully used control. It is documented only on Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X, electronic throttle, around 2005): idle at least 1000 rpm above target with the control already at zero for 2 or 5 s sets the code with the warning lamp at once, and a fail-safe cuts fuel to cylinders to stop the engine racing. GM and Ford use P0506/P0507 instead; CARB's mandatory limit is +200/−100 rpm.

causes.label: False air behind the throttle (intake, gasket, vacuum hose)
Throttle or idle valve stuck open (foreign body, coking)
Throttle actuator motor faulty (follow-on P2101)
Follow-on fault of other codes (sensors, pedal)

symptoms: Idle far above target, engine races
Jerking from cylinder cut-off in limp mode

P051A.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P051A.description: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051A is the sensor's general circuit fault. Ford uses it only for the digital SENT sensor, when the module receives invalid messages or signal patterns (together with U060E for lost communication); analogue sensors report P051B–P051D instead. It is checked continuously with 5 s to fault.

causes.label: Connector or supply, ground or SENT signal wire open or corroded
Sensor electronics faulty
Oil or moisture in the connector
Engine module

P051B.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P051B.description: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051B is its plausibility check. Ford flags a zero-point deviation above 0.15 inHg (about 0.5 kPa) from ambient with the engine stopped, and in operation at low air flow a pressure above 5 inHg (about 17 kPa) or below −0.6 inHg – so Ford also reports a real excess crankcase pressure under P051B. Maserati and Alfa Romeo bulletins name blow-by valves or software.

causes.label: Sensor zero point drifting
PCV or blow-by valve sticking, ventilation blocked or frozen (real overpressure)
Engine module software (known false trigger)
Increased blow-by from engine wear

symptoms: Possibly oil leaks or oil mist (real overpressure)

P051C.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P051C.description: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051C means the signal of the analogue ratiometric sensor is too low – Ford sets it below 0.44 V for 5 s. Typical is a signal shorted to ground, an open or shorted 5 V reference, or an open signal line pulled down.

causes.label: 5 V reference or signal line open or shorted to ground
Connector corroded or oily
Sensor faulty
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor

P051D.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P051D.description: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051D means the signal is too high – Ford sets it above 4.56 V for 5 s. Typical is a signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage, an open sensor ground, or an open signal pulled up. A real excess pressure in the crankcase does not set P051D.

causes.label: Sensor ground open
Signal line shorted to positive
Sensor faulty
Engine module

P051E.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P051E.description: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051E means the signal jumps or briefly drops below or above its limits – physically impossible changes, usually from a loose contact. No manufacturer document available to us uses P051E; Ford, Maserati and FCA use only P051A–P051D. The description follows CARB's input component rules.

causes.label: Loose contact at the sensor connector
Chafed harness
Oil or water in the connector
Sensor faulty internally

P051F.title: PCV Filter Restriction
P051F.description: The crankcase ventilation has an oil mist separator or filter element that can clog; the crankcase pressure sensor then sees rising pressure at a given flow. P051F reports this restriction. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – Ford reports high pressure under P051B. BMW and GM bulletins describe the consequences of a blocked separator: oil pushed past seals, oil mist in the intake and charge air cooler, higher oil consumption. CARB requires the PCV system to be monitored.

causes.label: Separator or filter clogged with oil, soot or sludge
Icing in the separator or hose on short winter trips
Oil change intervals exceeded (sludge)
Pressure sensor reading wrong

symptoms: Oil leaks at seals or dipstick
Oil mist in the intake, higher oil consumption

P0520.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0520.description: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0520 is the general circuit fault, used differently: Ford petrol and diesel engines set it for the digital SENT sensor when it reports an internal fault, does not initialise or sends values out of range (lost communication is U0600), after 5 s. GM's 1.4 L turbo with an oil pressure switch sets it when the switch reports pressure although the engine has been off long enough to be pressureless – type C, without warning lamp.

causes.label: Sensor or switch faulty internally
Connector corroded or oily (oil creeping through a leaking sensor)
Signal line open or shorted to ground
5 V reference or supply faulty (usually with other sensor codes)

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Oil pressure gauge or warning wrong
Cam phasing or cylinder deactivation possibly disabled

P0521.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Range/Performance
P0521.description: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0521 is the plausibility check. With the engine off the sensor must read about zero (GM: above 40 kPa after 10 s is a fault, Ford diesel above 70 kPa); with it running the value is compared with a model of speed and oil temperature (GM single-stage pump ±50 kPa). GM checks two-stage pumps against limits per stage and calibrates P0521 with the pump valve – so a real pressure fault can also set it. GM type B, two trips.

causes.label: Sensor drifting or stuck (offset)
Oil pump control valve or two-stage pump stuck in the wrong stage
Wrong viscosity, low oil level or foaming oil
Worn oil pump or bearings

symptoms: Oil pressure reading implausible or fluctuating
Cylinder deactivation or cam phasing possibly disabled

P0522.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Low
P0522.description: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0522 means the signal voltage is below its limit: GM 2018 below 5 % of the 5 V reference, Ford petrol below 0.25 V, Ford diesel below 0.018 V, about 5 s. As the sensor gives about 0.5 V at zero pressure, this is an electrical fault – real low pressure is P0524. GM's 2006 V8s used the warning lamp only with cylinder deactivation; GM's 4.6 L Northstar then allows cam phasing only above 1500 rpm.

causes.label: Signal line shorted to ground or open
5 V reference failed or shorted
Sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or oily

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Oil pressure gauge at zero or warning despite normal pressure
Cam phasing or cylinder deactivation possibly disabled

P0523.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A High
P0523.description: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0523 means the signal voltage is above its limit: GM 2018 above 95 % of the 5 V reference, GM 2006 above 4.89 V, Ford petrol above 4.75 V, Ford diesel above 4.992 V, about 5 s. Typical are an open sensor ground or a signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage. Real excess pressure is not reported here – Ford uses P055F for that. GM's 2006 V8s used the warning lamp only with cylinder deactivation.

causes.label: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Oil or moisture in the connector

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Cam phasing or cylinder deactivation possibly restricted

P0524.title: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low
P0524.description: P0524 is not a sensor fault but a condition: the measured oil pressure is below a minimum depending on speed, load and temperature (Ford diesel 30–90 kPa) for about 5 s, with the sensor itself plausible. Its purpose is engine protection; Ford petrol engines with mid-lock cam phasers drive them into the locked position. GM's tables do not use it; FCA updated the Ram EcoDiesel software against false setting in the cold. Stop the engine, check the oil level and confirm with a mechanical gauge.

causes.label: Oil level too low, oil loss or consumption
Too thin oil, fuel dilution or clogged pick-up screen
Oil pump or pressure control valve faulty or stuck
Worn crankshaft or camshaft bearings
False setting by software in the cold (Ram EcoDiesel)

symptoms: Oil pressure warning and/or check engine light

P0525.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0525.description: P0525 concerns vehicles with a separate cruise control servo – a vacuum or electric actuator on the throttle cable driven by the engine module: the control circuit is electrically sound, but the response does not match the command. With electronic throttle the engine module controls the throttle itself, so the code hardly applies there. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0525. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis: switching it off as the default reaction suffices, so usually no warning lamp.

causes.label: Servo worn or sticking, cable misadjusted
Vacuum leak at hose or diaphragm (vacuum servo)
Wiring, connector or fuse to the servo
Brake or clutch switch interrupting the servo release

symptoms: Cruise control inoperative or switches off

P0526.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit
P0526.description: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0526 means no usable signal although the clutch is driven: GM Duramax below 500 rpm with fan duty at least 36 % for 2 s; the 6.6 L LML distinguishes a level stuck low or high; GM petrol V8s set it when no pulses arrive with the engine running. Type B, two trips. GM also reports a missing signal under P0526. A GM bulletin for 2011–2013 Duramax vans and pick-ups names loud fan noise and weak air conditioning at low speed.

causes.label: Hall sensor at the fan clutch faulty
Wiring or connector (chafing at the shroud, corrosion)
Clutch not turning despite command
Engine module or supply

symptoms: Fan permanently on or off, loud fan noise
Weak air conditioning at low speed, overheating under load

P0527.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0527.description: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0527 means a signal is present but implausible – spikes, jumps or a speed that does not fit the clutch command and engine speed. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0527; GM covers implausibility through P0483 (target versus actual) and P0493. CARB requires input components used by other diagnoses to be checked for plausibility.

causes.label: Sensor or trigger element damaged, wrong air gap
Interference or ground fault on the sensor line
Viscous clutch slipping or sticking (real speed off)

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0528.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0528.description: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0528 means no pulses arrive from the sensor although the fan should be turning. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0528 – GM detects exactly this state (fan below 4 rpm with the engine running) but reports it as P0526. CARB requires input components to be checked for open and short circuits.

causes.label: Sensor faulty
Wire open or connector off
Fan or clutch really not turning

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Fan permanently on or not at all

P0529.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0529.description: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0529 means the speed signal drops out or jumps at times. It is documented only for Ford's 6.7 L Power Stroke in the 2016–2019 Super Duty and F-650/750: a Ford service message lists it with P0480, P0494, P0495 and P0691–P0694 for fans running permanently or not at all, and warns against replacing the clutch too early – check wiring, connector and sensor first. Ford's summaries give no thresholds.

causes.label: Loose contact at connector or wiring at the fan (vibration, chafing)
Sensor in the fan clutch intermittently faulty
Clutch itself faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Fan running permanently or not at all

P052A.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P052A.description: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index. Warning lamp after two trips; afterwards the normal cam codes take over. P052A means bank 1 was too far advanced. Outside cold start, P0011 applies.

causes.label: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain

symptoms: Possibly rattle or rough idle on cold start

P052B.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
P052B.description: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index. Warning lamp after two trips; afterwards the normal cam codes take over. P052B means bank 1 was too far retarded – typical for a phaser stuck in its locked base position.

causes.label: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing (stuck in base position)
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain

symptoms: Possibly rattle or rough idle on cold start

P052C.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
P052C.description: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index. Warning lamp after two trips; afterwards the normal cam codes take over. P052C means bank 2 of a V engine was too far advanced. Outside cold start, P0021 applies.

causes.label: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing (bank 2)
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain

symptoms: Possibly rattle or rough idle on cold start

P052D.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
P052D.description: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index. Warning lamp after two trips; afterwards the normal cam codes take over. P052D means bank 2 of a V engine was too far retarded. Outside cold start, P0022 applies.

causes.label: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing (bank 2)
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain

symptoms: Possibly rattle or rough idle on cold start

P052E.title: PCV Regulator Valve Performance
P052E.description: P052E is a function fault of the crankcase ventilation pressure regulating valve. Audi's 3.0 TFSI has a diaphragm valve whose torn diaphragm or elbow causes false air and whistling; Mercedes' M270/M274 have a switched part-load ventilation valve that blocks with oil carbon and lets oil into the intake – blue smoke, rough running, lack of power; Mercedes extended the emission warranty on the intake module. GM Europe's 2.0 diesel in the Saab 9-5 uses P052E differently, for PCV heater performance – which J2012 lists as P053D.

causes.label: Diaphragm of the regulating valve torn or fatigued
Part-load ventilation valve blocked (oil carbon, sludge)
Elbow or hose at the valve cracked, clamp leaking
Engine module software

symptoms: Whistling or hissing in the engine bay
Rough idle, blue smoke or oil consumption, lack of power

P052F.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage
P052F.description: Diesel glow plugs are switched by a separate glow plug control module fed from the battery, with its own ground, a command from the engine module and a diagnostic line back. P052F means its supply voltage is out of range. Ford's 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke set it below 6.5 V, above 16.5 V or with an open supply, after about 1 s, continuously. An FCA bulletin shows P052F together with all six glow plug open codes P0671–P0676, because without supply no current flows – check main feed, connector and grounds first. GM does not use it.

causes.label: Main feed to the module open or high-resistance (fuse, connector, corroded ring terminal)
Poor ground of the glow plug module
System voltage too low or too high (weak battery, regulator fault)
Glow plug module faulty internally

symptoms: Hard cold start, long cranking, white smoke
Several glow plug codes at once

P0530.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P0530.description: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0530 is the general circuit fault; GM and the Saab 9-4X use the more precise P0532/P0533 instead. Saab's 2006 9-5 diesel (Bosch EDC16) assigns P0530 differently, to a short to ground below 0.1 V for 0.6 s, switching off the A/C relay. Warning lamp depends on the maker.

causes.label: Connector or contacts corroded or loose
Pressure sensor faulty
Wire open or chafed
5 V reference shorted by another sensor

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0531.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0531.description: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0531 means the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the expected pressure. GM compares the pressure rise after compressor engagement with a model of ambient and coolant temperature, road speed and fan speed, 100 samples of 100 ms, type X without warning lamp. Saab's 2006 9-5 diesel assigns P0531 differently, to a short to positive above 4.9 V with 101 kPa substitute value.

causes.label: Pressure sensor drifting or stuck
Refrigerant charge wrong (too little or too much)
Compressor or control valve delivering poorly
Condenser dirty or fan weak

P0532.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P0532.description: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0532 means the signal voltage is too low – GM below 3 % of the 5 V reference in 80 of 100 samples (about 2 s), from a signal shorted to ground, an open signal line or a lost 5 V reference; an empty system at ambient pressure usually still reads in range. The compressor is locked out. Warning lamp: GM type C without, Saab 9-4X with, Ford depending on vehicle.

causes.label: Signal line open or shorted to ground
Pressure sensor faulty
Connector corroded or loose
5 V reference shorted or failed

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0533.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P0533.description: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0533 means the signal voltage is too high – GM above 98 % of the 5 V reference in 80 of 100 samples, from a signal shorted to positive or an open sensor ground. Real very high pressure normally leads to a pressure cut-out within range instead. The compressor is locked out. Warning lamp: GM type C without, Saab 9-4X with, Ford depending on vehicle.

causes.label: Signal line shorted to positive (e.g. 5 V reference)
Sensor ground open
Pressure sensor faulty internally
Extreme overpressure (overcharge, blocked condenser, fan off)

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P0534.title: A/C Refrigerant Charge Loss
P0534.description: P0534 reports too little refrigerant (a leak), not a sensor circuit: the module compares pressure or temperature in the circuit with a model, and the compressor is locked out for protection. FCA's 2020 Ram EcoDiesel sets it with the warning lamp; a software update fixed false setting. In GM's Volt, Spark EV and Lyriq the circuit also cools the traction battery – GM prescribes recovering and weighing the charge (Volt at least 800 of 950 g) and comparing the battery's refrigerant temperature sensors with ambient.

causes.label: Refrigerant leak (condenser, joints, compressor shaft seal, service ports)
Pressure or temperature sensor offset (misjudgement)
Software or calibration
Traction battery chiller faulty (electric and hybrid only)

symptoms: Air conditioning weak or not cooling
Check engine light or high-voltage service message (electric)

P0535.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0535.description: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0535 is the general circuit fault; the compressor is usually locked out or run with a substitute value. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.

causes.label: Sensor faulty
Connector corroded by condensate
Wire open or shorted
Engine module

symptoms: Air conditioning not or weakly cooling

P0536.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0536.description: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0536 means the signal is valid but implausible – for example it differs from other temperature sensors after standstill, or does not drop after compressor engagement. Hella compares it with the cabin sensor with A/C off. Icing protection then works wrongly. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.

causes.label: Sensor drifting
Sensor not seated correctly in the evaporator
Refrigerant shortage or compressor fault
Contact resistance in the connector

P0537.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0537.description: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0537 means the signal voltage is below its limit; with the usual NTC voltage divider that is a signal shorted to ground or a shorted sensor, read as implausibly warm – icing protection may then fail. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.

causes.label: Signal line shorted to ground
Sensor shorted internally
Condensate in the connector (leakage to ground)
Engine module

symptoms: Compressor permanently on or locked out

P0538.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0538.description: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0538 means the signal voltage is above its limit – an open sensor, signal or ground line, or a short to positive; with an NTC that reads as implausibly cold, so the system assumes icing and usually locks out the compressor. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.

causes.label: Connector off or corroded, wire open
Sensor open internally
Ground line open
Short to positive

symptoms: Air conditioning not cooling (compressor locked out)

P0539.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0539.description: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0539 means short dropouts or jumps in the signal that do not add up to a lasting low or high fault – usually a loose contact or condensate corrosion at the connector; the compressor may switch off at times. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the connector
Broken wire from movement or chafing
Sensor with internal intermittent contact

P053A.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit/Open
P053A.description: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053A means its control circuit is open. GM's diesels of 2016 check it with 20 of 40 samples below 90 °C coolant without warning lamp, GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI in the Saab 9-5 with the lamp on the first trip – a difference even within GM. The heater then has no effect, which only matters in hard frost.

causes.label: Heating element burnt out
Connector or wire open, corrosion
Fuse of the ignition supply blown
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
In frost: oil leaks or loss of power from frozen ventilation

P053B.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Low
P053B.description: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053B means the low-side control line is shorted to ground, so the heater stays on regardless of command – it works in frost, but heats permanently. GM's diesels of 2016 check it with 20 of 40 samples below 90 °C coolant without warning lamp, GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI in the Saab 9-5 with the lamp on the first trip – a difference even within GM.

causes.label: Control line chafed against ground
Heating element shorted to its housing
Engine module driver shorted

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P053C.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit High
P053C.description: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053C means the control line is shorted to positive: the driver cannot switch, the heater stays off, or the driver overloads and switches off. GM's diesels of 2016 check it with 20 of 40 samples below 90 °C coolant without warning lamp, GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI in the Saab 9-5 with the lamp on the first trip – a difference even within GM.

causes.label: Control line shorted to 12 V
Heating element shorted internally (very low resistance, overcurrent)
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
In frost: oil leaks or loss of power from frozen ventilation

P053D.title: PCV Heater A Performance
P053D.description: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053D means the heater is electrically connected but its effect or current is implausible – current outside the target window, an overheated driver, or the expected warming does not occur. No manufacturer document available to us uses P053D; GM Europe checks this function under P052E. Frost protection is then uncertain.

causes.label: Heating element aged (resistance outside 6–10 Ω, Saab reference)
Increased contact resistance at the connector
Partial short in the element (overcurrent, driver overheating)
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
In frost: oil leaks or loss of power from frozen ventilation

P053E.title: Crankcase Pressure Too High
P053E.description: P053E is the system code for crankcase pressure above an operating-point limit while the sensor itself is plausible. Normally the crankcase runs at a slight vacuum (GM: −1 to −5 inH2O). No manufacturer document available to us uses P053E – Ford reports the same under P051B (above 5 inHg at idle air flow). Excess pressure pushes oil past seals and the dipstick, carries oil mist into the intake and raises oil consumption. CARB requires the PCV system to be monitored.

causes.label: Ventilation or oil separator blocked or frozen
Pressure regulating or PCV valve faulty
Increased blow-by (piston rings, turbo oil side)
Leaking vacuum reservoir or pump in the valve cover

symptoms: Oil leaks at seals, dipstick pushed out

P053F.title: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 1
P053F.description: Petrol direct-injection engines often inject twice after a cold start, once late in the compression stroke, to heat the catalyst; this needs rail pressure within a window. P053F reports that the window was not reached often enough. Documented only by Ford's EcoBoost: over the whole cold-start phase it compares the time in the window with the phase duration against 0.70, once per cold start, with fuel level at least 15 % and the fuel sensors sound. The module then drops this mode, the catalyst lights off later; warning lamp after two trips. GM does not use P053F.

causes.label: High-pressure pump weak or volume control valve sluggish
Low supply pressure (lift pump, filter)
Rail pressure sensor drifting
Pump follower or cam lobe worn
Software or calibration

symptoms: Possibly longer cranking or rough cold idle

P0540.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit
P0540.description: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. Cummins checks it by the manifold temperature rise, Iveco by the battery voltage dip when the relay switches. P0540 is the general circuit fault of heater A without low/high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

causes.label: Heater relay faulty (contacts welded or burnt, solid-state relay shorted)
Heating grid burnt out
Power cable or ring terminal corroded or overheated, control connector
Engine module driver

symptoms: Hard cold start, white smoke, rough cold idle
With welded relay: battery drained, heater stays on

P0541.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low
P0541.description: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. Cummins checks it by the manifold temperature rise, Iveco by the battery voltage dip when the relay switches. P0541 means the voltage in the monitored circuit stays too low – typically a control line or relay coil shorted to ground or open, so the relay does not switch and there is no preheating. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

causes.label: Relay control line shorted to ground (chafing)
Relay coil open or solid-state relay faulty
Connector at relay or module corroded
Engine module driver

P0542.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High
P0542.description: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. P0542 means the voltage stays high although the heater is commanded on – a control line shorted to positive or a relay that does not switch. A shorted or welded relay can also power the heater permanently; Ram recalled 6.7 L Cummins trucks because a shorted heater relay could start a fire. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

causes.label: Heater relay faulty (solid-state relay shorted, contacts stuck)
Control line shorted to positive, harness chafed on a power cable
Power circuit overheated, cable scorched
Engine module driver

symptoms: Battery drained when heater stays on
Burning smell or scorched wiring at the relay

P0543.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Open
P0543.description: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. P0543 means an open circuit at heater A – in the control line or relay coil, or depending on the maker in the power circuit or heating element itself. It is detected by driver diagnosis with the output off, by a missing voltage dip on switching on or by a missing temperature rise. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

causes.label: Heating grid burnt out
Relay coil or contact open
Broken cable, loose nut or ring terminal at the grid
Fusible link in the heater circuit

symptoms: White smoke or knocking while warming up

P0544.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0544.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P0544 is the general fault of bank 1 sensor 1. Ford's 6.7 L diesel uses it not as a circuit fault but for plausibility against an exhaust temperature model: after at least 6 h off it compares sensor and model over 200–400 s, a fault exceeding ±80 °C for 20 s, once per trip. GM's Duramax does not use P0544. The module then runs on a model value and may restrict filter regeneration.

causes.label: Sensor aged or drifting, soot on the tip
Cable or connector damaged by heat or vibration
Exhaust leak before the sensor
Exhaust temperature really deviating (injection fault)

symptoms: Particulate filter regeneration missing, filter warning

P0545.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0545.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P054A.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P054A.description: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054A means bank 1 was too far advanced. Mercedes (M276) traces it to slow oil pressure – 1 bar should be reached after about 3 s; Audi (Q5 3.2) and VW (Atlas 3.6 and 2.0 T) fixed it by software.

causes.label: Oil pressure building too slowly when cold (oil level, viscosity, pick-up, pump)
Exhaust oil control valve sticking or screens clogged
Module software (threshold too tight)
Cam phaser defective, locking pin
Timing chain stretched or misassembled

symptoms: Check engine light on, usually without noticeable symptom

P054E.title: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Lower Than Expected
P054E.description: Diesel only. At controlled idle the module compares the fuel quantity the idle governor needs for target speed with a model value; CARB sets the limit from 2013 at ±50 % of what a sound engine needs. Ford's diesel sets the codes beyond ±50 % for 5 s at standstill with warm engine and no filter regeneration; GM compares with 0.5 times a minimum map or 1.5 times a maximum map, 200 of 255 samples, type B. P054E means the engine holds idle with much less fuel than expected – more energy arrives than commanded, for example from injectors delivering too much, oil entering combustion or wrong injector correction codes.

causes.label: Injectors delivering more than commanded (drift, coking, leaking needle)
Oil entering combustion (turbo seal, crankcase ventilation)
Rail pressure actually higher than measured
Wrong injector correction codes after replacement

symptoms: Blue or white smoke, knocking at idle

P054F.title: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Higher Than Expected
P054F.description: Diesel only. At controlled idle the module compares the fuel quantity the idle governor needs for target speed with a model value; CARB sets the limit from 2013 at ±50 % of what a sound engine needs. Ford's diesel sets the codes beyond ±50 % for 5 s at standstill with warm engine and no filter regeneration; GM compares with 0.5 times a minimum map or 1.5 times a maximum map, 200 of 255 samples, type B. P054F means the governor needs much more fuel than expected – the commanded quantity does not arrive or the engine has extra losses: clogged injectors, low compression, an EGR valve stuck open or additional load from accessories.

causes.label: Injectors delivering too little (coked, high return flow)
Rail pressure actually lower, fuel supply (filter, air)
Mechanical losses: compression, seizing accessories
EGR valve stuck open or intake blocked

P0550.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit
P0550.description: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0550 is the general circuit fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Without the signal the engine can drop or stall at full lock, or the module raises idle permanently as a substitute.

causes.label: Connector or wire open or corroded (splash zone at the pump)
Sensor or switch faulty, often also leaking
5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Idle drops when steering at standstill, engine may stall

P0551.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P0551.description: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. Mitsubishi sets it when the switch stays on through 10 drive-and-stop cycles; Saab's Trionic T8 after 600 s above 50 km/h, keeping raised idle as substitute and without warning lamp.

causes.label: Pressure switch stuck closed or faulty internally
Signal line shorted to ground (ground means active)
Permanently high pressure (steering valve sticking, kinked line)
Vehicle speed signal faulty (Saab depends on P0501)

P0552.description: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. P0554.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent
P0554.description: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. P0555.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0555.description: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. That makes it an input to idle and throttle control. P0555 is the general circuit fault without low/high distinction. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM splits circuit faults into P0557 and P0558. The module then assumes a substitute value and keeps vacuum available as a precaution.

causes.label: Connector or wire to the sensor open or corroded
Sensor faulty
5 V reference disturbed (short at another sensor on the same reference)
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light or brake booster warning

P0556.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0556.description: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. On direct-injection, turbo, stop-start and hybrid engines intake vacuum is scarce, so the engine module watches it and creates vacuum when needed – closing the throttle, suppressing engine stop or running an electric vacuum pump. Sensor stuck or drifting
Electric vacuum pump or its relay weak (hybrid, Porsche, turbo DI)
Module software (false setting)
Booster diaphragm leaking

symptoms: Check engine light and/or brake booster warning
Hard brake pedal with real vacuum loss

P0557.description: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. Sensor faulty

P0559.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0559.description: The brake booster pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal, ground) measures the vacuum in the brake booster. Sensor with internal dropouts

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)

P055A.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit
P055A.description: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055A is the general circuit fault without low/high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – GM reports sensor B only as P055B–P055D. The module then uses a substitute value and may set cam phasers or valve lift to their base position.

causes.label: Connector or harness to sensor B open, corroded or oily
Sensor B open internally
Shared 5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted

P055B.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B Range/Performance
P055B.description: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055B compares sensors A and B with the phasers almost idle: GM sets it when they differ by more than 220 kPa below 1850 rpm, 80 of 100 samples. causes.label: Sensor B drifting or stuck
Sensor A wrong (comparison fails because of A)
Real pressure difference: clogged screen, oil level or quality
Contact resistance in the connector

symptoms: Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted

P055C.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B Low
P055C.description: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. Documented only by GM (type B, two trips); Ford uses no sensor B. P055C means the signal is too low – an open 5 V supply or signal line or a short to ground, not low oil pressure. causes.label: 5 V supply or signal open, connector loose or corroded
Signal shorted to ground (chafing)
Sensor B faulty internally
Module's 5 V reference disturbed

symptoms: Cam phasing or valve lift switching possibly restricted

P055D.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch B High
P055D.description: Oil pressure sensor B is a second sensor, usually in the oil feed to the cam phasers or valve lift switching – on GM's 2.5 L (2014 Impala and Malibu) in the camshaft cover – while sensor A measures the main gallery. causes.label: Sensor ground open

Sensor B faulty internally
Engine module
