P055E.title: Oxygen Sensor Control Module System Voltage
P055E.description: Some engines use wide-band or NOx sensors with their own evaluation module that reports over CAN. That module measures its supply; outside its working range it sets P055E, and lambda control and the sensor diagnoses are suspended because no valid values exist. No manufacturer document available to us uses P055E – Ford's diesel monitors the comparable supply of its smart NOx/O2 sensor as P220A/P220B, below 8.5 V or above 16.5 V. CARB requires modules delivering emission-relevant signals to be monitored.

causes.label: Fuse, relay or supply line to the sensor module
Poor module ground
Battery or alternator (under- or overvoltage)
Sensor module faulty

symptoms: Lambda control in open loop, possibly higher consumption

P055F.title: Engine Oil Pressure Out of Range
P055F.description: P055F is a condition code: the measured oil pressure is above the maximum expected for speed and oil temperature – Ford, which documents it, calls it 'too high' and pairs it with P0524 (too low). Ford checks continuously for 5 s, only with plausible oil pressure, oil temperature and coolant sensors, as engine protection. Background are regulated oil pumps, whose control valve (P06DA ff) defaults to full pressure on failure. An electrically high signal is P0523 or P055D instead.

causes.label: Oil pump control valve or variable pump stuck at high pressure
Pump relief valve stuck
Wrong viscosity, very cold oil
Sensor A reading high within range

symptoms: Check engine light or oil pressure warning
Possible engine protection or power limit
Possible oil filter or seal leaks

P0560.title: System Voltage
P0560.description: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0560 is the general code without low/high split, used differently: Saab's 2002 9-5 transmission module sets it below 9 V or above 18 V for 1 s and goes into limp mode; Saab's EDC16 diesel only above 17 V (24 V charger or jump start); the GM-built 9-4X as a low-voltage code. GM's and Ford's engine modules use P0562/P0563 instead.

causes.label: Battery weak or faulty
Alternator or regulator (under- or overcharging)
Jump start or charger at 24 V
Corroded or loose battery terminals or ground strap

symptoms: Several modules report codes, starting problems

P0561.title: System Voltage Unstable
P0561.description: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. GM interprets P0561 as a difference between the module's two supply inputs: permanent battery and switched ignition supply may differ by at most 3 V, otherwise it sets after 50 of 63 samples. In the engine module that is type C without warning lamp, in GM's 9-speed transmission module type A with the lamp after one trip. Other makers use it for a fluctuating voltage.

causes.label: Fuse, relay or line of the ignition supply (voltage drop)
Loose or corroded connector or ground at the module
Voltage regulator fluctuating
Battery terminal loose

symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light (GM transmission module)

P0562.title: System Voltage Low
P0562.description: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0562 means the voltage is below its threshold with the engine running, when the charging system should deliver: GM 9 V or less at 400 rpm or more in 400 of 500 samples (about 5 s), type C. Saab's 9-4X modules may switch off temporarily below about 9 V. Many other modules, such as GM's brake module, set P0562 themselves.

causes.label: Alternator or regulator delivering too little
Battery faulty (shorted cell)
Corroded terminals, ground straps or alternator cable
High quiescent current or many consumers at idle

P0563.title: System Voltage High
P0563.description: The module measures its own supply voltage. CARB allows other monitors to be suspended below 11 V, and above a maker's threshold only if the voltage itself is diagnosed – that is what these codes record. GM's engine modules and Ford's PCM set them without warning lamp. P0563 means the voltage is above its threshold: GM's engine module 18 V or more in 400 of 500 samples, type C; Saab's 9-4X above 18 V for 5 s. causes.label: Regulator or alternator overcharging

Missing battery or poor battery terminal (voltage spikes)

P0564.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit
P0564.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0564 watches signal line A of the ladder: only voltage windows matching a button or no button are valid. GM sets it when the ratio sits in a gap between windows for over 0.5 s (2014: 2.5 s), the body module in the Saab 9-4X and 9-5 after an invalid voltage for 2 s. Cruise control is locked out for the ignition cycle.

causes.label: Cruise or steering wheel switch faulty or dirty (moisture, worn contacts)
Clockspring or steering wheel connector with contact resistance
Supply or signal line to the body module open or shorted
Body module

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be switched on or switches off
No check engine light, engine runs normally

P0565.title: Cruise Control On Signal
P0565.description: Cruise control buttons are almost always a resistor ladder on one or two signal lines, each button giving its own voltage; the module reading it (GM and Saab from about 2010: the body module; FCA: steering column module or PCM) sends the button state to the engine module over CAN. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis – it is simply switched off – so GM lists all these codes as type C and Ford as non-MIL: no warning lamp, the engine runs normally. P0565 concerns the on signal. GM sets it when the on/off button is reported pressed for over 20 s. P056E.title: Cold Start Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Performance

Engine or body module

P057A.description: The brake pedal position sensor is an analogue 5 V sensor, usually Hall-type, giving the pedal position continuously instead of a switch – for brake lights, cruise control, stop-start, brake-throttle override and regenerative braking. 5 V reference, signal or ground line open
Sensor faulty internally
Engine or body module

P057B.description: The brake pedal position sensor is an analogue 5 V sensor, usually Hall-type, giving the pedal position continuously instead of a switch – for brake lights, cruise control, stop-start, brake-throttle override and regenerative braking. Typically the compressor is blocked and the fan runs. GM rates sensor A faults without the lamp, the Saab 9-4X with it.

Radiator fan runs unnecessarily or irregularly

P05E2.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P05E2.description: The refrigerant pressure sensor (three wires, 5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) tells the engine module the A/C pressure; it uses it to switch the radiator fan, to block the compressor at too high or too low pressure and to pre-control idle load. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility, but they need not light the lamp if they do not affect emissions. 'Intermittent/Erratic' means the signal jumps implausibly fast or briefly leaves its valid range without staying low or high long enough for those codes. Chafed or broken harness
Sensor B faulty
5 V reference or control module

Warning lamp depending on the maker

P05E3.title: Park Brake Sensor/Switch Circuit
P05E3.description: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. Faulty diode in the switch circuit (Volvo)

P05E8.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit/Open
P05E8.description: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05E8 means the control circuit is open: the driver sees missing voltage or high resistance.

causes.label: Connector at the valve loose, corroded or spread
Valve solenoid coil open
Broken wire in the harness
Output driver in the module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light (if rated as emission related)
Oil too hot under load or slow warm-up, depending on rest position

P05EB.title: Cold Start SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P05EB.description: After a cold start a diesel heats its exhaust actively – retarded and post injection, intake or exhaust throttling, higher idle, EGR cooler bypass – so the SCR catalyst quickly reaches the temperature at which urea dosing can start (around 180–200 °C). P05EB sets when the measured temperature at the SCR inlet stays below the expected or modelled value within a set time after the start: the heating strategy is not working. CARB requires this 'catalyst warm-up' monitor for light-duty diesels from model year 2026 (20 %) to 2028 (100 %); GM 2025 and Ford 2023 tables do not contain the code yet. Volvo Trucks used it on 2016–17 heavy-duty engines and advised a software check instead of replacing parts. The lamp comes on; no power limitation from this code alone is known.

causes.label: Engine module software or calibration (false trigger)
Exhaust temperature sensor before the SCR reads low or slow
Heating measure not effective: throttle, EGR cooler bypass or turbo vanes sticking
Post or retarded injection not effective (injectors)
Exhaust leak before the sensor or extremely cold conditions

symptoms: Higher NOx emissions after cold start (not noticeable)

P05EC.title: Cold Start Injection Timing Performance
P05EC.description: To heat the exhaust after a cold start, a diesel shifts its start of injection, usually later, plus post injections. CARB requires faults of such elements during the cold start strategy to be reported under codes separate from normal operation – hence P05EC. GM's 2025 diesels compare the start of injection requested by the application software with the timing actually scheduled for the injector drivers, during cold start only; a deviation beyond ±4 or ±5 in 88 of 176 or 8 of 16 samples sets the code and the lamp in the first trip. Ford's 2023 diesel instead checks whether the cold start operating mode is really activated when requested (10 s). Mechanical injector timing faults in normal operation are P01CB ff and P020A ff; the petrol counterpart for ignition timing is P050B.

causes.label: Engine module software or internal fault (request and execution differ)
Cold start mode blocked by other faults (coolant or fuel temperature, rail pressure)
Injector driver or injector circuit
Weak battery during cold start

symptoms: Possibly more white smoke or rougher running after cold start

P05ED.title: Reductant Heater Control Module Supply Voltage
P05ED.description: Some diesels use a separate control module or power stage for the DEF heaters in tank, pump and lines; without heating, frozen fluid cannot thaw in winter and dosing stays blocked. P05ED reports that this module's supply voltage is outside its allowed window – a blown main fuse, an open feed or ground, or system voltage too low or too high. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Thresholds are not published; GM's L5P monitors the comparable heater supply under its own codes and flags a drop of more than 3 V below battery voltage while heating is requested. Start with fuse, feed, ground and battery or charging system.

causes.label: Main fuse or feed wire to the heater module faulty, connector corroded (splash zone)
Poor module ground
Weak battery or charging fault (system voltage too low or too high)
Heater control module faulty internally

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
In cold weather: DEF frozen, dosing blocked, further heater codes

P05EE.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P05EE.description: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05EE means the supply circuit is open: when the supply is switched on, no voltage or current reaches the pump branch. Ford's comparable check flags a pump controller voltage below 6 V. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes.label: Connector at the pump or tank module corroded or loose
Open wire in the harness to the tank
Fuse or relay of the pump supply faulty
Pump or tank module open internally

symptoms: DEF/AdBlue warning, possibly countdown to no-restart
Follow-up codes for low DEF pressure or SCR efficiency

P05EF.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P05EF.description: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

P05F3.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
P05F3.description: A power relay, switched by the engine module through an output driver, feeds aftertreatment consumers such as the DEF pump, tank and line heaters and possibly NOx sensors or the SCR module. P05F8.title: Reductant Heater Control Module Performance
P05F8.description: P05F8 is the function check of the DEF heater control module: its feedback does not match the command – heating current or power, temperature rise, or an internal module fault. The code is documented for Chrysler's 3.0 L EcoDiesel in the 2014 Ram 1500 and Jeep Grand Cherokee: several bulletins list it together with the heater codes P20BA, P20BE and P20C2, and the fix in each case was only reprogramming the engine module – a diagnostic that was too sensitive rather than a hardware defect. Unstable module supply or ground

P05F9.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit
P05F9.description: A discrete stop-start status line tells the engine module (or another module) whether stop-start is active, inhibited or has just stopped the engine. On most current cars this status travels over CAN instead, so a hard-wired line and these codes are rare; no manufacturer document available to us uses P05F9–P05FB. CARB names stop-start as its example of an 'emissions neutral' reaction: a module that simply disables stop-start when a fault appears may report it without the check engine light, which is what Ford does for its stop-start codes. P05F9 is the general circuit fault or open line. The typical reaction is that stop-start is disabled; the driver-operated stop-start switch has its own codes.

causes.label: Open status line or connector problem
Sending module without supply or faulty
Wrong software or variant coding (stop-start set without hardware)

symptoms: Stop-start indicator or message in the cluster
Check engine light only with some makers

P05FA.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit Low
P05FA.description: A discrete stop-start status line tells the engine module (or another module) whether stop-start is active, inhibited or has just stopped the engine. On most current cars this status travels over CAN instead, so a hard-wired line and these codes are rare; no manufacturer document available to us uses P05F9–P05FB. CARB names stop-start as its example of an 'emissions neutral' reaction: a module that simply disables stop-start when a fault appears may report it without the check engine light, which is what Ford does for its stop-start codes. P05FA means the status line stays below its lower limit – a short to ground or a missing pull-up supply. Stop-start is then disabled.

causes.label: Status line shorted to ground
Sending module pulls the line to ground permanently (faulty output)

P05FC.title: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 2
P05FC.description: During a cold start, direct injection petrol engines usually raise rail pressure for finer atomisation with multiple injections while the catalyst heats up. P05FC monitors whether the actual rail pressure of bank 2 stays within the target window during this phase – only engines with separate rails and pressure sensors per bank (V or boxer engines with two high-pressure circuits) can set it. CARB lists fuel pressure as a cold start component that must respond measurably beyond what would happen without the strategy. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05FC; Ford checks the single-rail counterpart P053F and flags a fault when the share of cold start time inside the pressure window is 0.70 or less, and Kia replaced the engine module of the 2018 Stinger 2.0T for P053F with stumbling during warm-up. GM uses P2C1E–P2C20 instead.

causes.label: High-pressure pump or volume control valve of bank 2 weak or sticking
Low supply pressure (low-pressure pump, filter)
Rail pressure sensor of bank 2 inaccurate
Engine module software
Leaking injector or pressure relief on bank 2

symptoms: Stumbling, hesitation or rough idle during warm-up

P05FD.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Temperature Too High
P05FD.description: Electric variable-geometry turbo actuators use a DC motor with gearing, driven by an H-bridge in the engine module or in the actuator itself. Constant high load – sooted or stiff vanes, running against a stop, an internal motor short – drives up current and temperature. GM's 2025 diesels set P05FD when the H-bridge driver exceeds 170 °C in 240 of 300 samples (about 3 s) and light the lamp in the first trip. The driver then shuts off for protection, the actuator stops or returns to its rest position, and boost control is limited – underboost or overboost and reduced power can follow. GM Europe's earlier 2.0 diesels reported the same protection under P0046. Circuit faults of the actuator are P0045–P0048, the position sensor P2563 ff.

causes.label: Vane mechanism sooted or stiff, actuator works constantly against resistance
Electric actuator faulty internally (shorted turns, bearing)
High ambient heat at the actuator (missing heat shield, exhaust leak)
Engine module or driver

symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

P05FE.title: Active Grille Air Shutter C Performance/Stuck Off
P05FE.description: Active grille shutters close the air inlet when little cooling is needed, to reduce drag and speed up warm-up. P05FE is the performance check of a third shutter C – target and actual position do not match, as P059F does for shutter A and P05AE for shutter B. Only vehicles with three separately driven shutters could set it, and no manufacturer was found that uses a shutter C: GM and Ford use only A (upper) and B (lower). This description therefore follows A and B: control is suspended and the shutter stays where it is or opens; if it sticks closed, cooling air is missing under load. GM and Ford light the lamp for A and B after two trips. Ice and debris are frequent causes, and GM fixed false A/B codes in snow by software on the 2025 Equinox. Stuck on is P2C73.

causes.label: Debris or ice blocking the louvres
Louvres unhooked or broken (impact)
Shutter C actuator faulty
Connector, wiring or supply corroded
Software false trigger in frost

symptoms: Check engine light (depending on the maker)
Higher coolant temperature under load or slower warm-up

P05FF.title: Brake Pressure Sensor/Brake Pedal Position Sensor Correlation
P05FF.description: Stop-start decides when to stop and restart the engine from the brake: Ford stops it when the pedal switch is on and master cylinder pressure is high enough, and restarts when pressure falls below a filtered reference. P05FF means brake pressure (from the sensor in the ABS unit, sent over the network) and brake pedal position do not agree – for example pedal pressed without pressure build-up, or pressure without pedal. Ford's 2020–23 petrol vehicles check this continuously in the section 'Brake Diagnostics for Stop-Start Dependability' and set the code within 1 s, without the check engine light; stop-start is blocked so the engine is not stopped or started unexpectedly. Ford gives no threshold for the deviation. GM monitors the pedal travel sensor under P057x instead. Brake switch disagreement is P0504.

causes.label: Brake pedal position sensor or switch misadjusted or faulty
Master cylinder pressure sensor in the ABS unit faulty
Network communication or software between ABS module and engine module
Air in the brake system or hydraulic fault (long pedal travel without pressure)

symptoms: No check engine light at Ford, possibly wrench or service warning
Possible related codes P0504 or brake pressure codes
